title: Detection by exact families of abelian functors
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories and F_i:C -> D additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Suppose an object X is zero whenever all F_i(X) are zero. Then the family detects zero maps and isomorphisms; a short complex in C is exact, respectively short exact, if and only if all its images are.

proof.text: Factor a map through its image. Exact functors preserve the epimorphism onto the image and its monomorphism into the codomain. If all image maps are zero, all image objects are zero; joint zero-object detection kills the original image. Apply this to differences for joint faithfulness. Cancellation detects mono and epi maps, hence isomorphisms. For exactness, use the composite kernel(g) -> cokernel(f). In each image it factors through the corresponding kernel-to-cokernel composite and vanishes. Joint faithfulness makes the original composite zero. Combine this with detected mono and epi maps for short exactness.

lean.statement:
theorem exact_family_detection {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] [Abelian D] {I : Type w}
    (F : I → C ⥤ D) [∀ i, (F i).Additive]
    [∀ i, PreservesFiniteLimits (F i)] [∀ i, PreservesFiniteColimits (F i)]
    (hz : ∀ X : C, (∀ i, IsZero ((F i).obj X)) → IsZero X) :
    (∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), (∀ i, (F i).map f = 0) → f = 0) ∧
    (∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), (∀ i, IsIso ((F i).map f)) → IsIso f) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.Exact ↔ ∀ i, (S.map (F i)).Exact) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact ↔ ∀ i, (S.map (F i)).ShortExact)
